campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 6, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council's October 6, 2026 agenda listed a mix of routine business and a few larger items, including a proclamation for Breast Cancer Awareness Month, approval of nearly $5.3 million in bills, and a resolution to seek an $8.5 million state parks grant. The agenda also listed salary and compensation adjustments for city management staff and the City Manager, along with appointments to two advisory bodies.
keyTopics: Proclamation recognizing October 2026 as Breast Cancer Awareness Month, honoring El Camino Health
Resolution to apply for an $8.5 million Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization grant
Resolutions adjusting compensation for unrepresented Confidential, Classified Management, and Unclassified Management employees, and a separate resolution adjusting the City Manager's salary
Acceptance of a $16,680 donation of motorized blackout shades for the Heritage Theatre from the Friends of the Heritage Theatre
Appointments to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee and the Civic Improvement Commission

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 7, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council's October 7, 2026 agenda covers routine business like meeting minutes, check registers, and the Treasurer's report, alongside several larger items. These include a major budget amendment for the Hakone Gardens koi pond renovation, a new no-parking zone on Chester Avenue, a decision on the city's long-term law enforcement provider, a comparison of animal care service options, and an annual update to city code provisions.
keyTopics: Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation Project budget amendment of $2,500,000
No Parking Anytime zone proposed for part of Chester Avenue near Arcadia Palms Drive
Discussion and determination of the City's long-term law enforcement provider, including a possible agreement with Los Gatos Monte Sereno Police Department
Comparison of regional animal care providers, including whether to continue with San Jose Animal Care and Services
Annual Code Update covering appeal scheduling, City Commissioner qualifications, and business record retention

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 22, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council agenda for September 22, 2026 includes a wastewater treatment plant agreement, a councilmember's reappointment to the VTA Board, a temporary moratorium on detention and custodial facilities, and appointments to several city commissions. The agenda also covers a legal services contract amendment and approval of prior meeting minutes.
keyTopics: Resolution authorizing Addendum No. 14 to the Regional Water Quality Control Plant Basic Agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View
Reappointment of Councilmember Jonathan Weinberg to the VTA Board for an additional two years
Interim urgency ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on detention or custodial facilities and custodial processing facilities
Appointments to the Complete Streets, Environmental, and Planning Commissions
Amendment to the legal services agreement with Berliner Cohen, LLP, setting a $21,500 monthly retainer for up to 70 hours plus a $385 hourly rate

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 6, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council's October 6, 2026 agenda covers mostly routine business, including approving prior meeting minutes, financial reports, and a purchasing policy update. It also includes a bid issue on a tree services contract and the Finance Commission's updated work plan.
keyTopics: Relieving Denali Tree Services of its bid due to a bidder's mistake
First amendment to a town agreement, authorized for execution by the Town Manager
Finance Commission's updated 2026 Work Plan
Resolution amending the Town's Purchasing Policy (Policy 4-06)
July 2026 expenditure and revenue reports

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — October 7, 2026
san-jose.summary: This is a San José Rules and Open Government Committee agenda for October 7, 2026. The October 13 meeting was cancelled, so items here mostly involve planning the October 20 draft agenda, along with several standalone reports and items, including a proclamation request and a proposed item on self-checkout safety standards at grocery and drug stores.
keyTopics: Review and setup of the October 20, 2026 draft agenda, including adding new items and assigning time-certain slots
Public Record covering September 24–October 1, 2026 from the City Clerk
Joint City of San José and Santa Clara Valley Water District special meeting item from the City Manager
City Auditor's Monthly Report of Activities for September 2026

Proposed proclamation and flag-raising event for Taiwan Retrocession Day (sponsored by Council District 5), and a proposed item on self-checkout safety standards for grocery and drug retail stores (Candelas and Cohen)

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee — September 29, 2026
mountain-view.summary: This Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee agenda covers the city's draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan and the 2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory. The meeting included options for the public to join and comment virtually or by phone.
keyTopics: Draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan
2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council's October 6, 2026 agenda includes several recognitions (Little League All-Stars, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week), routine consent items, and public hearings on nonfunctional turf watering restrictions and a service worker retention ordinance. The agenda also lists approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation and informational reports on completed council priority projects.
keyTopics: Public hearing and ordinance introduction to prohibit potable water use for irrigating nonfunctional turf, implementing state law AB 1572 (CEQA exempt under Section 15307)
Discussion and possible action to introduce a Service Worker Retention Ordinance
Approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation
Amending a purchase agreement with WSP USA Inc. for environmental consulting at the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill, raising the not-to-exceed amount to $385,000

Informational reports on completed projects: eliminating chemical pesticide use on city property, an artificial turf policy study, and feasibility of converting PG&E-owned lots near Ramona, Lois, and Dona Avenues into a linear park

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 6, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council's agenda for October 6, 2026 includes closed-session items on potential litigation and real estate negotiations with the Cupertino Union School District over the Finch Avenue property, plus a recognition item for the Community Development Department. The public agenda also lists routine consent items, a resolution to acquire the Finch property via exchange for $11.8 million, a public information session on soil contamination remediation at The Rise, and a TEFRA hearing on conduit financing for The RISE development.
keyTopics: Closed-session discussion of anticipated litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue with Cupertino Union School District
Recognition of the Community Development Department (Planning, Building, Housing, and Code Enforcement Divisions)
Resolution to increase employer PEMHCA medical contributions for certain retired annuitants
Approval of an exchange agreement for the Finch property at a negotiated purchase price of $11.8 million
Public information session on approved soil contamination remediation plan at The Rise, followed by a TEFRA hearing on conduit financing for the project

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council and Authorities Concurrent — October 6, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council and Stadium Authority Board have a joint agenda for October 6, 2026, starting with a dinner meeting with the Parks and Recreation Commission, followed by a regular meeting covering proclamations, routine consent items, and several substantive policy discussions. Key topics include pedestrian access restrictions on local expressways, Stadium Authority finances, and a major focus on data center development policy, alongside multiple councilmember requests about data centers and parking issues.
keyTopics: Report and potential Council action on pedestrian access restrictions on portions of Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways
Stadium Authority Financial Status Report for Quarter Ending June 30, 2026 and related budget amendments
Staff presentation on a comprehensive approach to updating city policies on data center development, including water usage and grid support
Councilmember Hardy's requests regarding data center entitlement/power allocation processes and a possible ban on non-disclosure agreements with stand-alone data centers

Councilmember Park's deferred requests on resident parking near apartment complexes, compensation for vehicles ticketed/towed during stadium events, and parking requirements for affordable housing projects

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council agenda for September 15, 2026 listed several financial and infrastructure items, including a draft federal housing/community development grant plan, a review of the red light camera safety program, and the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The agenda also included resolutions related to the city's former redevelopment agency, including a bond refinancing item.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency board
Resolution for the sale and issuance of refunding bonds for the Successor Agency

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — October 2, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee's agenda for October 2, 2026 includes staff and committee member comments, and an update on the city's electric system long-duration resiliency efforts. A late packet report was added, with an accompanying staff presentation, noting the item is not a project under CEQA.
keyTopics: Update on Electric System Long Duration Resiliency
Late packet report added, with staff presentation, regarding CEQA status (Not a Project)
